title: Original selection after a layered fault
summary: Hold per-start fallback latches across Official Panels, Skills, Workflows, Point Libraries, Tool Programs, and reviewed agent modules. A layered Official package that breaks at run time gets a fresh Host of its shipped artifact and records a break in LucBreaker; another Luc's Panel that breaks while it fills a workspace role gives the module back to the role's own Panel for the rest of the start.

replaceability.why: The adapter and layering machinery are the Host foundation. If this machinery could be replaced by a creator layer, automatic fallback to the original could not be guaranteed. The Lucs carried by open protocols have their own replacement classes.
replaceability.decided: Acrab, self-Luc spec v0.3, 2026-10-18; interface charter rule 6, 2026-10-22

reach.notes: Trusted Host machinery, not authority granted to a Luc. Package calls remain bounded by their resolved permissions, Host APIs and editable scope.

operations.name: fall_back
operations.notes: No deadline. Returns false for no original, non-Panel, stale page hash, mixed protocols, or original resolve/load refusal. First successful report counts one break and latches; repeat returns same answer without recount. A Panel of a Luc with no layers that fills a workspace role (iface:editor.placement/v1) gives the module back instead, when its page hash is current and the role's own Panel is loaded: the answer names the role's own Luc and the other Luc as its one layer, tripped false, and nothing is counted by the breaker.

operations.name: panel_source

output.description: Tuple (original Host, entries stripped of layers) after fallback; otherwise (active Host, entries).

operations.notes: No deadline is enforced by this synchronous Python seam. Retrying a read observes the current state.

operations.name: fallen_seats

output.description: Capability id -> {code} for every Panel of another Luc that broke in use in a workspace role at this start.

operations.notes: The Worker passes it to workspace_catalog, panel_document and panel_call so a broken role Panel is neither placed nor served.

operations.name: fell_back_at

output.description: When the Panel gave way at this start (UTC, ending in Z), for its one luc.module_fell_back event.

operations.notes: Called only after fall_back answered fell_back true for the same capability id.

operations.name: note_agent_break
operations.notes: No deadline. First latch returns true, repeat false; does not itself increment persistent breaker. Worker counts under lumeri.agent.instructions using the artifact_hash.

operations.name: agent_fallback

output.description: None, or layer{id,version} and code; no internal notified_sessions set.

operations.notes: No deadline is enforced by this synchronous Python seam. Retrying a read observes the current state.

operations.name: layers_held

output.description: None or code=E_LUC_LAYER_TRIPPED with layer ids and versions where known.

operations.notes: No deadline is enforced by this synchronous Python seam. Retrying a read observes the current state.

invariants.text: Stale document hashes do not change the active source or breaker.
A valid fault restores the exact shipped Panel and repeated reports do not count it twice.
Another Luc's Panel that breaks in a role gives the module back to the role's own Panel; a page from before gives nothing back, and repeated reports give the same answer and count no break.
Without the role's own Panel loaded a broken role Panel gives nothing back, and the editor's own view takes over.

break: The operation rejects invalid input, integrity, authority or binding state as described by its operation.

conformance.notes: Verified across Panels, Skills, Workflows, Point Libraries, Tool Programs, and workspace roles.

known_deviations.text: Notices are best effort. Panel and agent payloads differ; event-store failure does not prevent the original from answering.

A role Panel's break holds for the start only and is not counted by luc_breaker, so the same Panel fills the role again at the next start and may break again; a layered Official Panel's breaks trip it after three.
A role Panel whose Luc has layers of its own first falls back to its Luc as shipped; if that page breaks too, the editor's own view takes over rather than the role's own Panel.
